en: Damn.
Damned.
Damn.
Damn.

ex.en: Darn it, I forgot my camera!
ex.ja: あ、カメラ忘れた！

ex.en: Although you can't compare them to Radiohead, Kashmir is a pretty darn good band.
ex.ja: ラジオヘッドとは比べるべくもないが、カシミールはなかないいバンドだよ。

note.ja: damn を婉曲にした語。「ちぇっ」。「繕う」は別語で語源ははっきりしない。

en: To cause an intense dislike for something.
An intense dislike or loathing someone feels for something bad or nasty.

disgust.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French desgouster, from Old French desgouster (“to put off one's appetite”), from des- (“dis-”) + gouster, goster (“to taste”), from Latin gustus (“a tasting”). By surface analysis, dis- + gust (“taste”).
The noun is from Middle French desgoust, from the verb.

ex.en: I always view this photo with disgust.
ex.ja: この写真を見るとむかつく。

ex.en: When it comes to raw fish, I feel disgusted.
ex.ja: 生の魚となると気分が悪くなってしまうのです。

ex.en: I am disgusted with myself for my short memory.
ex.ja: 忘れっぽいのには自分ながら呆れる。

note.ja: dis（反対）+ gustus（味）。「味がまずい」→「嫌悪・むかつかせる」。gusto（味わい・楽しみ）と同じ。

en: The termination of an organized body or legislative assembly, especially a formal dismissal.
Disintegration, or decomposition into fragments.

dissolution.ety: From Middle English dissolucioun, from Old French dissolucion, from Latin dissolūtiō (“a dissolving, destroying, breaking up, dissolution”).

ex.en: Justice without mercy is cruelty; mercy without justice is the mother of dissolution.
ex.ja: 哀れみのない正義は冷酷である。しかし、正義のない哀れみは解体の母である。

note.ja: dis（ばらばらに）+ solu（解く）+ tion。解きほぐすこと →「解散・解消・分解」。

en: The act of disturbing, being disturbed.
Something that disturbs.

disturbance.ety: From Middle English disturbaunce, from Old French destorbance, destourbance, from destourber (“disturb”), from Latin disturbō. By surface analysis, disturb + -ance.

ex.en: The police intervened in the disturbance.
ex.ja: 警察が騒動に介入した。

note.ja: dis（ひどく）+ turb（かき乱す）+ ance。かき乱すこと →「騒ぎ・妨害・障害」。

en: Something that is enclosed, i.e. inserted into a letter or similar package.
The act of enclosing, i.e. the insertion or inclusion of an item in a letter or package.

enclosure.ety: From Middle English enclosure, from Old French enclosure, from enclore, from Latin inclūdere, inclūdō, from in- (“in”) + claudō (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- (“key, hook, nail”). Alike to inclusion. By surface analysis, enclose + -ure.

ex.en: There are many kinds of animals inside this enclosure.
ex.ja: この囲いの中には何種類もの動物がいます。

note.ja: en（中に）+ clos（閉じる）+ ure。中に閉じ込めること →「囲い地・同封物」。

en: Pertaining to the doctrines or teachings of the Christian gospel or Christianity in general.
Pertaining to the gospel(s) of the Christian New Testament.
A member of an evangelical church.
An advocate of evangelicalism.

evangelical.ety: From evangelic + -al, from Old French evangelique, from Latin evangelium, from Ancient Greek εὐαγγέλιον (euangélion, “good news”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 euangelion（よい知らせ・福音）から。eu（よい）+ angelos（使者）。「福音主義の」。angel と同じ。

en: Especially or extraordinarily fine or pleasing; exceptional.
Recherché; far-fetched; abstruse.

exquisite.ety: From Latin exquīsītus (“to be outsought”), perfect passive participle of exquīrō (“to outseek”).

ex.en: This is an exquisite little painting.
ex.ja: これは小さくて極めて美しい絵画だ。

ex.en: This soup is exquisite.
ex.ja: なんておいしいスープなんだろう。

ex.en: The tourists were fascinated with the exquisite scenery.
ex.ja: 観光客達はその素晴らしい風景にうっとりした。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ quis（求める）+ ite。探し求めて選び出された →「この上なく美しい・精巧な」。

en: Pertaining to or consisting of objective claims.
True, accurate, corresponding to reality.
Programmes having content based on facts, such as documentaries.

factual.ety: From fact + -ual, modeled after, and by analogy with, actual.

note.ja: fact（事実）+ -ual。fact はラテン語 factum（なされたこと）。「事実に基づく」。

en: In a false manner.

falsely.ety: From Middle English falsly, falsliche, equivalent to false + -ly.

ex.en: I was falsely accused.
ex.ja: 濡れ衣を着せられた。

ex.en: Tom was falsely accused.
ex.ja: トムは濡れ衣を着せられた。

note.ja: false（偽りの）+ -ly。ラテン語 falsus（だまされた）。「誤って・偽って」。

en: Extreme shortage of food in a region.
A period of extreme shortage of food in a region.

famine.ety: Borrowed from Middle French famine, itself from the root of Latin fames.

ex.en: These countries were often visited with famine.
ex.ja: これらの国はしばしば飢饉に襲われた。

ex.en: That is why so many people are suffering from famine.
ex.ja: それが、こんなに多数の人が饑饉で苦しんでいる理由です。

ex.en: War has produced famine throughout history.
ex.ja: 戦争は歴史上ずっと飢餓を引き起こしてきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 fames（飢え）から。「飢饉」。famished（飢えた）も同じ。

en: Dishonest; based on fraud or deception.
False, phony.

fraudulent.ety: From Middle English fraudulent, from Old French fraudulent, from Latin fraudulentus, from fraus (“fraud”).

ex.en: Please beware of fraudulent emails.
ex.ja: 騙りメールにご注意ください。

ex.en: Please exercise every caution against cowboy salesmen of water purifiers and fraudulent-test sales.
ex.ja: くれぐれも浄水器の悪質訪問販売業者や無料点検商法にはご注意ください。

note.ja: fraud（詐欺）+ -ulent。ラテン語 fraus（ごまかし）。「詐欺の・不正な」。

en: A highway with grade-separated crossings (rather than level crossings) and designed (and only permitted) for high-speed motor-traffic run…
A toll-free highway.

ex.en: There was a terrible accident on the freeway.
ex.ja: 高速道路で悲惨な事故があった。

ex.en: He came by the freeway.
ex.ja: 彼は高速道路を通ってやってきた。

ex.en: There are roads and freeways wherever you go in America.
ex.ja: アメリカでは、どこへ行っても立派な道路と高速道路がある。

note.ja: free（無料の・妨げのない）+ way（道）。「信号のない高速道路」。

en: Recently, newly.
In a rude or impertinent manner.

freshly.ety: From Middle English freschely, freschliche (also as ferscheli, fersly, ferselich), equivalent to fresh + -ly.

ex.en: They sell us freshly caught fish in the early morning market.
ex.ja: 彼らは捕り立ての魚を朝市で売ってくれる。

ex.en: I like the smell of freshly-baked bread.
ex.ja: 焼きたてのパンの匂いが好きです。

ex.en: The fish is freshly caught.
ex.ja: とれたての魚です。

note.ja: fresh（新鮮な）+ -ly。「〜したての」（freshly baked：焼きたての）。

en: A newspaper; a printed sheet published periodically.
An official periodical publication published by a government containing legal and state notices, and in some cases, legislations, subsidi…
To publish (something) in a gazette.
To announce the status of (someone) in an official gazette; this pertained to both appointments and bankruptcies.

gazette.ety: Borrowed from French gazette, from Italian gazzetta, from Venetan gazeta, from gazeta dele novità (literally “a gazeta (halfpenny) of news”), named for the cost (one gazeta) of the newspaper. Compare penny dreadful, dime novel. See gazzetta for more.

note.ja: イタリア語 gazzetta（小銭）から。ヴェネツィアで新聞が小銭1枚で売られたことから「新聞・官報」。

en: A person who is intensely interested in a particular field or hobby and often having limited or nonstandard social skills. Often used wit…
An expert in a technical field, particularly one having to do with computers.
To perform bizarre and unpleasant feats as part of a carnival.
To enthusiastically engage in geek-like or nerdy interests.

geek.ety: Started as carnival slang, likely from the British dialectal term geck (“a fool, dupe, simpleton”) (1510s), apparently from Dutch gek or Low German geck, from an imitative verb found in North Sea Germanic and Scandinavian meaning "to croak, cackle," and also "to mock, cheat" (Dutch gekken, German gecken, Danish gække, Norwegian gakke, Swedish gäcka). The root still survives in the Dutch adjective noun gek (“crazy" or "crazy person”). Compare gink and also Old Norse gikkr (“a pert, rude person; jester; fool”).

ex.en: Tom is a math geek.
ex.ja: トムは数学オタクです。

ex.en: Tom is a language geek.
ex.ja: トムは言語オタクだ。

note.ja: ドイツ語・オランダ語の geck（ばか）から。「変わり者」→「オタク」。

en: A grandmother.
Any elderly woman, regardless of if she has grandchildren.
Typically or stereotypically old-fashioned, especially in clothing and accessories worn by or associated with elderly women.
To be a grandmother.
To act like a stereotypical grandmother; to fuss.

granny.ety:
Etymology tree
English gran(nam)
Proto-Germanic *-j-, *-ij-
Proto-West Germanic *-i, *-ī
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English granny
From gran(nam) + -y.

ex.en: Our granny is an expert at pickling foods.
ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃん、漬物名人なのよ。

ex.en: The baby reacted by saying "Granny."
ex.ja: 「ばあば」と赤ちゃんは反応した。

ex.en: "Where's Granny?" "In the kitchen."
ex.ja: 「おばあちゃんどこ？」「台所よ」

note.ja: grandmother の幼児語。「おばあちゃん」。

en: Something that prevents, hampers, or hinders.
An allowance of a certain amount of time or distance in starting, granted in a race (or other contest of skill) to the competitor possess…
To encumber with a handicap in any contest.
To place at disadvantage.

handicap.ety: From hand-in-cap, in reference to holding the game stakes in a cap.

ex.en: Having no will is the worst handicap.
ex.ja: 意志を持たない事が最悪の不利だ。

ex.en: You can get over the handicap soon.
ex.ja: すぐにその困難は乗り越えられるよ。

ex.en: The blind young man has got over his handicap.
ex.ja: 目の不自由なその青年はハンディキャップを克服した。

note.ja: hand in cap（帽子の中に手）から。昔の物々交換の賭けで、帽子の中に金を入れて公平にしたことから「不利な条件・ハンディキャップ」。

en: A demonstration of respect, as towards a person after his or her retirement or death.
An artistic work imitating another in a flattering style.

homage.ety: From Middle English homage, from Old French homage, hommage, from Medieval Latin homināticum (“homage, the service of a vassal or 'man'”), from Latin homō (“a man, in Medieval Latin a vassal”) + -āticum (noun-forming suffix). The American pronunciations in /-ɑːʒ/ and with silent h are due to confusion with the nearly synonymous doublet hommage, which is indeed pronounced /oʊˈmɑːʒ/.

ex.en: Hypocrisy is the homage that vice pays to virtue.
ex.ja: 偽善とは悪徳が徳に対して払う忠順の誓いである。

note.ja: 古フランス語 homage（家臣の誓い）から。homme（人・家臣）。「臣従の礼」→「敬意・オマージュ」。

en: The state of being hostile.
A hostile action, especially a military action. See hostilities for specific plural definition.

hostility.ety: From Middle English hostilitie, hostilite, from Old French hostilité, from Latin hostīlitās. By surface analysis, hostile + -ity.

ex.en: I have no personal hostility to the system.
ex.ja: その制度に対する個人的な敵意はない。

ex.en: Hostility was replaced by love.
ex.ja: 敵意に代わって愛情が生まれた。

note.ja: hostile（敵意のある）+ -ity。ラテン語 hostis（敵・よそ者）。「敵意・戦闘」。host（もてなす人）と同系。

en: A song of praise or worship, especially a religious one.
To sing a hymn.
To praise or extol in hymns.

hymn.ety: From Middle English ymne, from Old English ymen (reinforced by Old French ymne), from Latin hymnus, borrowed from Ancient Greek ὕμνος (húmnos).

ex.en: The morning service began with a hymn.
ex.ja: 朝の礼拝は賛美歌ではじまった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hymnos（神をたたえる歌）から。「賛美歌」。n は発音しない。

en: Based upon a hypothesis; conjectural.
Conditional; contingent upon some hypothesis/antecedent.
A possible or hypothetical situation or proposition.

note.ja: hypothesis（仮説）+ -tical。ギリシャ語 hypo（下に）+ thesis（置くこと）。「仮定の」。

en: Providing information; especially, providing useful or interesting information.
Of a standard or specification, not specifying requirements, but merely providing information.

informative.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂

English -ative
English informative
From inform + -ative.

note.ja: inform（知らせる）+ -ative。「有益な」。

en: A violation or breach, as of a law.
An encroachment on a right, a person, a territory, or a property.

infringement.ety:
Etymology tree
English infringe
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥tom
Proto-Italic *-mentom
Latin -mentum
Old French -mentbor.
Middle English -ment
English -ment
English infringement
From infringe + -ment.

ex.en: Notwithstanding their own repeated scandals, the police continue to nonchalantly issue infringement tickets.
ex.ja: 相次ぐ不祥事にも関わらず、警察はオメオメ違反切符を切っている。

note.ja: infringe（侵害する）+ -ment。in + frangere（壊す）。「（権利を）壊すこと」→「侵害」。fragile、fraction と同じ frag。

en: A job taken by a student in order to learn a profession or trade.
The first year of a medical residency.

internship.ety:
Etymology tree
English intern
Proto-Germanic *skapjaną
Proto-Germanic *-skapiz
Proto-West Germanic *-skapi
Old English -sċiepe
Middle English -schipe
English -ship
English internship
From intern + -ship.

ex.en: My internship is coming to an end.
ex.ja: インターンシップが終わろうとしています。

ex.en: I'm going to do an internship at a local company.
ex.ja: 現地企業でのインターンシップを体験する。

ex.en: I applied for a summer internship.
ex.ja: 夏のインターンシップに応募しました。

note.ja: intern（実習生）+ -ship。「インターンシップ」。

en: Causing irritation, annoyance or pain.
Stimulating or exciting a response.

ex.en: He is a very irritating critic of others.
ex.ja: 他人のあらばかり探す嫌な人である。

ex.en: Far from irritating my skin it was better than before I used it.
ex.ja: 肌がヒリつくどころか、使う前より肌が安定してるんです。

ex.en: His pretentiousness is irritating.
ex.ja: 彼のきざな態度は頭にくる。

note.ja: irritate（いらいらさせる）+ -ing。ラテン語 irritare（刺激する・怒らせる）。「いらいらさせる」。

en: Any of several plants, of the genus Jasminum, mostly native to Asia, having fragrant white or yellow flowers.
The perfume obtained from these plants.

jasmine.ety:
Etymology tree
Middle Persian yʾsmn'
Classical Persian یَاسَمِین (yāsamīn)bor.
Arabic يَاسَمِين (yāsamīn)bor.
French jasminbor.
English jasmine
Borrowed from French jasmin, from Arabic يَاسَمِين (yāsamīn).

ex.en: Is this jasmine tea?
ex.ja: これってジャスミン茶？

note.ja: ペルシャ語 yāsaman から。「ジャスミン」。

en: The act of making one unconscious, or at least unable to come back on one's feet within a certain period of time; a TKO.
The deactivation of anything.
Rendering someone unconscious.
Amazing; gorgeous; beautiful.

ex.en: He won the fight by a knockout.
ex.ja: 彼はノックアウト勝ちした。

note.ja: knock out（打ち倒す）の名詞化。「ノックアウト」→ 打ちのめされるほどすばらしい人・物。

en: A case of translucent or transparent material made to protect a flame, or light, used to illuminate its surroundings.
Especially, a metal casing with lens used to illuminate a stage (e.g. spotlight, floodlight).
To furnish with a lantern.
Of a facial feature, large and squarish in shape as an old-fashioned lantern.

lantern.ety: From Middle English lanterne (13th century), via Old French lanterne from Latin lanterna (“lantern”), itself a corruption of Ancient Greek λαμπτήρ (lamptḗr, “torch”) (see lamp, λάμπω (lámpō)) by influence of Latin lucerna (“lamp”). The spelling lanthorn was current during the 16th to 19th centuries and originates with a folk etymology associating the word with the use of horn as translucent cover. For the verb, compare French lanterner to hang at the lamppost. Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-container”).

ex.en: Tom held up the lantern.
ex.ja: トムはランタンを掲げた。

ex.en: The forest was illuminate​d by a lantern.
ex.ja: ランタンが林を照らした。

ex.en: Lanterns are floated to worship Great God Kuzuryū.
ex.ja: 九頭竜明神を祭るために灯篭をながす。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 lamptēr（たいまつ）から。lampein（輝く）。lamp と同じ。

en: Thread or cloth made from flax fiber.
Domestic textiles, such as tablecloths, bedding, towels, underclothes, etc., that are made of linen or linen-like fabrics of cotton or ot…
Made from linen cloth or thread.
Having the colour linen, light beige.

linen.ety: From Middle English lynnen, lynen, from Old English līnen (“linen", "made of flax”), from Proto-West Germanic *līnīn (“made of flax”), from Proto-Germanic *līną (“flax”), from Proto-Indo-European *līno- (“flax”), equivalent to line + -en. Cognate with Latin līnum (“flax”) and thus also Linum. More at line.

ex.en: Let's not wash our dirty linen in public.
ex.ja: うちの恥をさらすな。

ex.en: Don't wash your dirty linen in public.
ex.ja: 汚い下着を人前で洗うな。

note.ja: 古英語 līnen（亜麻の）から。ラテン語 linum（亜麻）。line（線 ＝ 亜麻糸）と同じ。

ja: 見張り（on the lookout：見張って）

en: A vantage point with a view of the surrounding area.
A session of watching for an approaching enemy, police, etc.

ex.en: They were on the lookout for a storm.
ex.ja: 彼らは嵐を警戒していた。

ex.en: The soldier kept a sharp lookout in the darkness.
ex.ja: 兵隊は暗闇で四方に目を配った。

ex.en: I think that it likely that there was a major fault in the lookout.
ex.ja: おそらく、見張りに重大な欠陥があったんではないかと考えています。

note.ja: look out（見張る）の名詞化。「見張り」。

en: Not comprehended correctly.
Not viewed with sympathy and understanding despite warranting it.

ex.en: Perhaps you've misunderstood the aim of our project.
ex.ja: もしかすると、あなたは私たちの計画の目的を勘違いしているのかもしれません。

ex.en: Anything that can be misunderstood will be.
ex.ja: 誤解され得るものはいずれすべて誤解されるであろう。

ex.en: Perhaps you have misunderstood the aim of our project.
ex.ja: もしかすると、あなたは私たちの計画の目的を勘違いしているのかもしれません。

note.ja: misunderstand の過去分詞。「誤解された」。

en: The light reflected from the Moon, which seems to emanate from it.
Chiefly in to do a moonlight: short for moonlight flit (“an act of secretly leaving premises without paying the rent, supposedly at night…
To do a moonlight flit: to secretly leave premises without paying the rent, supposedly at night by the light of the Moon.
To make a night-time attack on a tenant farmer not supporting the policies of the Irish National Land League.

ex.en: The couple walked holding hands in the moonlight.
ex.ja: 二人は手を取り合って月明かりの中を歩いた。

ex.en: The island showed black in the moonlight.
ex.ja: 島は月光の中に黒々と見えた。

ex.en: The two held hands and walked in the moonlight.
ex.ja: 二人は手を取り合って月明かりの中を歩いた。

note.ja: moon（月）+ light（光）。「月光」→ 夜にこっそりする仕事 →「副業をする」。

en: The largest member of the deer family (Alces americanus, sometimes included in Alces alces), of which the male has very large, palmate an…
Any of the extinct moose-like deer of the genera Cervalces and Libralces.

moose.ety: Earlier mus, moos, from an Eastern Algonquian language name for the animal, such as Massachusett moos, mws, Narragansett moos or Penobscot mos (cognate to Abenaki moz), from Proto-Algonquian *mo·swa (“it strips”), referring to how a moose strips tree bark when feeding: compare Massachusett moos-u (“he strips, cuts smooth”).

note.ja: アメリカ先住民アルゴンキン語族の言葉から。「ヘラジカ」。

en: A small flying insect of the family Culicidae, the females of which bite humans and animals and suck blood, leaving an itching bump on th…
To fly close to the ground, seemingly without a course.

Borrowed from Spanish mosquito (“gnat”), diminutive of mosca (“fly”), from Latin musca (“fly”), from Proto-Indo-European *mūs- (“fly, stinging fly, gnat”). Cognate with West Flemish meuzie (“mosquito”), dialectal Swedish mausa (“fly”), Lithuanian musė (“a fly”) and Sicilian muschitta (“midge”). See also midge. First attested in the 1580s.

ex.en: This net here is to keep off mosquitoes.
ex.ja: この網は蚊を寄せ付けないためのものだ。

ex.en: I shut the window to keep the mosquitoes out.
ex.ja: 私は蚊を入れないよう窓を閉めた。

ex.en: I hate mosquitoes, but they seem to love me.
ex.ja: 私は蚊が大っ嫌いなんだけど、蚊は私のことが大好きみたいね。

note.ja: スペイン語 mosquito（小さなハエ）から。mosca（ハエ）+ 縮小。

A low-cost short-stay hotel, often with hourly rates rather than daily rates, and notorious for permitting illicit sexual activities; a l…
To stay in a motel or motels.

To convert a word to a noun.

ex.en: In Esperanto, nouns always end with "o".
ex.ja: エスペラントの名詞は、必ず「o」で終わります。

ex.en: Role-Language includes male and female collective nouns in Japanese.

ex.en: It's OK to think of 'five minutes' as a noun phrase, right?
ex.ja: 「five minutes」って名詞句でいいんですよね？

note.ja: ラテン語 nomen（名前）から古フランス語を経た語。nom（名前）の仲間。名前を表す語 →「名詞」。

ex.ja: その小説家は私達の世代でかなり人気がある。

ex.ja: 私の人生の目標は小説家になることです。

ex.ja: 焦らず、一歩一歩歩むことが大切です。

en: To bring about the downfall of (a government, etc.), especially by force; to usurp.
A removal, especially of a ruler or government, by force or threat of force; usurpation.

overthrow.ety:
From Middle English overthrowen, equivalent to over- + throw. Compare Dutch overdraaien, German überdrehen, Old English oferweorpan (“to overthrow”).
For the noun sense, compare Middle English overthrow, overthrowe (“destruction, downfall”), from the verb.

ex.en: The government was overthrown.
ex.ja: 政府は倒された。

ex.en: I will overthrow the dictator.
ex.ja: 独裁者を倒すのだ！

ex.en: The ruler was overthrown and banished from the country.
ex.ja: 支配者は打倒され国外に追放された。

note.ja: over（ひっくり返して）+ throw（投げる）。「投げ倒す」→「打倒する・転覆させる」。

en: A pattern, a way of doing something; especially a pattern of thought, a system of beliefs, a conceptual framework.
An example serving as the model for such a pattern; an exceptionally good or prototypical example of a pattern or group.

paradigm.ety: From Middle English paradygme, from Late Latin paradīgma, from Ancient Greek παράδειγμα (parádeigma, “pattern”), from παραδείκνυμι (paradeíknumi, “I show [beside] or compare”) + -μα (-ma, suffix forming nouns concerning the results of actions). Doublet of paradigma.

ex.en: We need to postulate a completely different paradigm to explain all these phenomena.
ex.ja: これらのすべての現象を説明するにはまったくの異なるパラダイムを立てる必要がある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paradeigma（見本）から。para（並べて）+ deiknynai（示す）。「見本・典型」→「枠組み」。

en: A paved surface; a hard covering on the ground.
A paved path, for the use of pedestrians, located at the side of a road.

pavement.ety: From Middle English pament, from Anglo-Norman pavement and reinforced by Middle French pavement; both from Latin pavīmentum (“paved surface or floor”), from pavīre (“to beat, to ram, to tread down”). Morphologically pave + -ment.

ex.en: A strange man was walking back and forth on the pavement.
ex.ja: 見知らぬ男が歩道を行ったり来たりしていた。

ex.en: One shouldn't ride a bicycle on the pavement.
ex.ja: 歩道で自転車に乗ってはいけません。

ex.en: Walk on the pavement.
ex.ja: 歩道を歩きなさい。

note.ja: pave（舗装する）+ -ment。ラテン語 pavire（突き固める）。「舗道・歩道」。

en: The day of the week or month, or the specific day, on which an employee's wages or salary is paid.

ex.en: Could you loan me some money until payday?
ex.ja: 給料日までお金を貸してもらえませんか？

ex.en: It is a payday today.
ex.ja: 今日は給料日である。

ex.en: Payday can't come soon enough.
ex.ja: 給料日、早く来ないかな。

note.ja: pay（給料）+ day。「給料日」。

en: Lasting forever, or for an indefinitely long time.
Set up to be in effect or have tenure for an unlimited duration.

perpetual.ety: From Middle English perpetuel, from Old French perpetuel, from Latin perpetuālis (“universal”), from perpetuus, from petō.

ex.en: You can see that mountain's perpetual snow from here.
ex.ja: ここからはあの山の万年雪が見えます。

ex.en: A contented mind is a perpetual feast.
ex.ja: 満ち足りた心は永遠の祝宴である。

ex.en: Lifelong education means perpetual retraining.
ex.ja: 生涯教育は絶え間ない再訓練を意味する。

note.ja: ラテン語 perpetuus（途切れない）から。per + petere（向かう）。「永久の」。perpetually と同じ。

The biology or form of a living organism.

The meat from this bird.
To deceive with a confidence game.

ex.en: There are many pigeons in the City Square.
ex.ja: その市の広場には鳩がたくさんいる。

ex.en: Have you ever seen a baby pigeon?
ex.ja: ハトの雛って見たことありますか？

ex.en: He used pigeons in his experiment.
ex.ja: 彼は実験にハトを使いました。

note.ja: ラテン語 pipio（ピーピー鳴くひな）から古フランス語を経た語。「ハト」。

en: A largely level expanse of land at a high elevation; tableland.
A comparatively stable level after a period of increase. (of a varying quantity)
To reach a stable level after a period of increase; to level off.

plateau.ety: Borrowed from French plateau, diminutive of plat (“a plate”); see plate. Doublet of platter.

ex.en: Divorce rates might reach a plateau soon.
ex.ja: 離婚率はやがて頭打ちになるでしょう。

ex.en: What is the altitude of the plateau?
ex.ja: その台地は標高どのくらいですか。

ex.en: It's pleasant to take a walk on the plateau.
ex.ja: 高原を散歩するのは楽しい。

note.ja: フランス語 plateau（平らな板）から。plat（平らな）。「高原」→ グラフの平らな部分 →「停滞期」。plate、platform と同じ。

en: A list of recorded songs scheduled to be played on a radio station.
A list of tracks or videos to be played in a particular sequence, as from an audio CD or a streaming service.
To include (a track) on a playlist.

ex.en: Eh? This tune ... The playlist has looped.
ex.ja: あれ？この曲・・・。プレイリストが一周してるな。

note.ja: play（再生する）+ list（一覧）。「再生リスト」。

en: An enclosed space having defined limits, normally marked by walls.
The general area surrounding a place, environs.

precinct.ety:
From Middle English precinct, precincte, early 15th century, in sense of “district for government purposes”, from Medieval Latin precinctum, alternative form of praecinctum (“enclosure, boundary line”), neuter singular of praecinctus, perfect passive participle of Latin praecingō (“surround, gird”), from prae (“before”) + cingō (“surround, encircle”), from which also cinch.
Cognate to Italian precingere (“to encircle”).

note.ja: ラテン語 praecinctum（囲まれた場所）から。prae + cingere（囲む）。「区域」→ 警察の「分署・管轄区」。

The act of increasing, rising, or proliferating; augmentation, amplification, enlargement, escalation, aggrandizement.

en: To start criminal proceedings against.
To charge, try.

prosecute.ety: Borrowed from Latin prōsecūtus, perfect participle of prōsequor. Doublet of pursue, from Old French. Compare also persecute.

Other than what is apparent; spurious; sham.
Insincere.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pseudēs（偽の）から。「偽の」。pseudonym（ペンネーム）。

en: Any of various dishes, sweet or savoury, prepared by boiling or steaming or from batter.
A type of cake or dessert cooked usually by boiling or steaming.

pudding.ety:
From circa 1305, Middle English podynge (“kind of sausage; meat-filled animal stomach”), puddynge, from Old French boudin (“blood sausage, black pudding”), from Latin botellus (“sausage, small intestine”). Doublet of boudin.
* An alternative etymology assumes origin from Proto-Germanic *put-, *pud- (“to swell”) (compare dialectal English pod (“belly”), Old English puduc (“wen, sore”), Low German puddig (“swollen”), Westphalian Puddek (“lump, pudding”), Puddewurst (“black pudding”). More at pout.

ex.en: The proof of the pudding is in the eating.
ex.ja: 論より証拠。

ex.en: How often do you eat pudding?
ex.ja: プリンって、どれぐらいの頻度で食べる？

ex.en: Peter remarked that the pudding was too sweet.
ex.ja: ピーターはそのプリンが甘すぎるといった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 boudin（腸詰め）からとされる。もとは肉の詰め物 →「プディング」。

en: A household or commercial appliance used for keeping food fresh using refrigeration.
A similar device used to keep non-food items cold, such as blood, photographic film, drugs, or pharmaceuticals like insulin.

ex.en: Leave it in the refrigerator until it sets.
ex.ja: 固まるまでそのままにしておくか冷蔵庫で冷やしてください。

ex.en: There isn't much butter left in the refrigerator.
ex.ja: 冷蔵庫にはバターがあまり残っていない。

ex.en: Is there anything to drink in the refrigerator?
ex.ja: 冷蔵庫に何か飲み物がありますか。

note.ja: re（再び）+ frigus（寒さ）+ -ator。「冷やすもの」→「冷蔵庫」。fridge はこの短縮。frigid（極寒の）も同じ。

en: Rebuilding or restructuring; large scale repair or renewal; revitalisation.
Spiritual rebirth; the change from a carnal or material life to a pious one

regeneration.ety: From re- + generation or regenerate + -ion, from Latin regenerātiō.

note.ja: re（再び）+ gener（生む）+ ation。再び生み出すこと →「再生・再開発」。

en: The act of remembering; a holding in mind, or bringing to mind; recollection.
The state of being remembered, or held in mind; memory, recollection.
To remember; to recall to mind.

remembrance.ety: From Middle English remembraunce, from Old French remembrance, from remembrer (“to remember”), from Late Latin rememorārī (“to call to mind, to remember”). Equivalent to remember + -ance.

ex.en: I have no remembrance of it now.
ex.ja: 私は今ではそれについてなにも覚えていません。

ex.en: It comes to my remembrance.
ex.ja: 私はそれを思い出します。

ex.en: The event is worthy of remembrance.
ex.ja: その事件は記憶する価値がある。

note.ja: remember（思い出す）+ -ance。「記憶・追悼」。Remembrance Day（戦没者追悼記念日）。

en: Of, or relating to reminiscence.
Suggestive of an earlier event or times.
One who is addicted to indulging, narrating, or recording reminiscences.

reminiscent.ety: From Latin reminīscēns, present participle of reminīscor (“remember”), from re- (“again”) + min-, base of me-min-isse (“to remember, think over”), akin to mens (“mind”); see mental, mind, etc.

note.ja: ラテン語 reminisci（思い出す）から。re + mens（心）。「思い出させる」。mental と同系。

en: Anger or displeasure stemming from belief that one or one's group has been wronged or betrayed by others; indignation.

resentment.ety: From resent + -ment, after Middle French and French ressentiment (in Old French as recentement), from an archaic usage of the verb ressentir via Old French sentir, from Latin sentiō, sentīre (“to feel”). Compare Italian risentimento, Portuguese ressentimento, and Spanish resentimiento. Doublet of resentiment and ressentiment, the former attested slightly earlier.

ex.en: The resentment runs deep.
ex.ja: 恨みは深いですよ。

ex.en: I feel resentment against your unwarranted criticism.
ex.ja: 僕は君の根拠のない非難に腹がたっているんだ。

ex.en: I felt resentment against my uncle for deceiving me.
ex.ja: よくも自分を欺いたなと、伯父に対して憤りを感じた。

note.ja: re（強く）+ sent（感じる）+ ment。強く感じ返すこと →「憤り・恨み」。

en: A viscous water-insoluble hydrocarbon exudate of certain plants, or such a substance as a component of a plant exudate; used in lacquers,…
Any synthetic compound of similar properties.
To apply resin to.

note.ja: ラテン語 resina（樹脂）から。「樹脂」。

en: Capable of rotation.
A roundabout, traffic circle.
Any of the clubs making up the international Rotary International movement for community service.

rotary.ety: Attested mid 18th century, from Medieval Latin rotarius, from Latin rota (“wheel”).

note.ja: ラテン語 rota（車輪）から。「回転する」→ ロータリー交差点。rotate と同じ。

en: Marked or corroded by rust.
Of the rust color, reddish or reddish-brown.

rusty.ety: From Middle English rusty, from Old English rūstiġ (“rusty”), from Proto-Germanic *rustagaz (“rusty”), equivalent to rust + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian rusterch (“rusty”), West Frisian rustich, roastich (“rusty”), Dutch roestig (“rusty”), German Low German rusterig, rüsterig (“rusty”), German rostig (“rusty”), Swedish rostig (“rusty”).

ex.en: I found an old rusty key in that room.
ex.ja: その部屋で古びた錆だらけの鍵を見つけました。

ex.en: You get rusty if you haven't spoken English for a long time.
ex.ja: やっぱりいつも英語を話していないと急に話そうとしても口がまわらないね。

ex.en: Would you scrape that rusty pan?
ex.ja: そのなべを磨いていただけませんか。

note.ja: rust（さび）+ -y。「さびた」→ さびついたように「腕が鈍った」。

en: Uncommon, rare; difficult to find; insufficient to meet a demand.
Scantily supplied (with); deficient (in); used with of.

scarce.ety:
From Middle English scars, scarse, from Old Northern French scars, escars ("sparing, niggard, parsimonious, miserly, poor"; > French échars, Medieval Latin scarsus (“diminished, reduced”)), of uncertain origin. One theory is that it derives originally from a Late Latin *scarpsus, *excarpsus, a participle form of *excarpere (“take out”), from Latin ex- + carpere; yet the sense evolution is difficult to trace. Compare Middle Dutch schaers (“scarce”), Middle Dutch schaers (“a pair of shears, plowshare”), scheeren (“to shear”).
The standard pronunciation having the /ɛə(ɹ)/ vowel instead of expecte

ex.en: Food is still scarce in the region.
ex.ja: その地域ではまだ食料が不足している。

ex.en: Water is scarce in this area.
ex.ja: この辺では水が不足しています。

ex.en: Rain is scarce in this country.
ex.ja: この国は雨がとぼしい。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 escars（乏しい）から。ラテン語 excerpere（選び出す）とされる。「乏しい・不足している」。scarcely と同じ。

en: One who simulates or feigns.
A machine or system that simulates an environment (such as an aircraft cockpit), often for training purposes.

en: Of a surface, having low friction, often due to being covered in a non-viscous liquid, and therefore hard to grip, hard to stand on witho…
Evasive; difficult to pin down.

slippery.ety: From Middle English slipperie, an extended form ( + -y) of Middle English slipper, sliper (“slippery”), from Old English slipor (“slippery”), from Proto-Germanic *slipraz (“smooth, slippery”), equivalent to slip + -er. Compare also Middle English slibbri, slubbri (“slippery”) borrowed from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German slibberich (“slippery”). Cognate with German schlüpfrig (“slippery”), Danish slibrig (“slippery”), Swedish slipprig (“slippery”).

ex.en: Watch your step. The floor is slippery.
ex.ja: 足元に注意して下さい。床がすべりやすいから。

ex.en: The floor is slippery, so be careful.
ex.ja: 床滑るから気をつけてね。

ex.en: The road is really slippery because of the rain.
ex.ja: 雨のせいで、道路がすごく滑りやすいんだ。

note.ja: slip（すべる）+ -ery。「滑りやすい」→ つかみどころのない。

en: To be saturated with liquid by being immersed in it.
To immerse in liquid to the point of saturation or thorough permeation.
An immersion in water etc.
A low-lying depression that fills with water after rain.

soak.ety: From Middle English soken, from Old English socian (“to soak, steep”, literally “to cause to suck (up)”), from Proto-Germanic *sukōną (“to soak”), causative of Proto-Germanic *sūkaną (“to suck”). Cognate with Middle Dutch soken (“to cause to suck”). More at suck.

ex.en: Tom got soaking wet and caught a cold.
ex.ja: トムはずぶ濡れになって、風邪をひいた。

ex.en: I was in a coffee bar soaking in the atmosphere.
ex.ja: 私はカフェバーで雰囲気に浸っていた。

ex.en: What happened? You're all soaking wet.
ex.ja: びしょ濡れじゃん。どうしたんだ？

note.ja: 古英語 socian（浸す）から。suck（吸う）と同系。「浸す・びしょぬれにする」。

en: An exciting or extraordinary scene, exhibition, performance etc.
Drama and excitement in a display, product, performance, exhibition, etc.

spectacle.ety: From Middle English spectacle, from Middle French spectacle, from Latin spectāculum (“a show, spectacle”), from spectō (“to see, behold”), frequentative of speciō (“to see”). See species. Doublet of spectaculum.

ex.en: The royal wedding was a great spectacle.
ex.ja: 王室の結婚式は大変な壮観だった。

ex.en: Almost one-third of all office workers wear spectacles.
ex.ja: 全会社員のほとんど３分の１の人が、眼鏡をかけている。

ex.en: He looked sharply at me over his spectacles.
ex.ja: 彼は眼鏡越しに私をにらみつけた。

note.ja: spect（見る）+ acle。見るべきもの →「光景・見もの」、複数形 spectacles は（見るための）「眼鏡」。

en: To be sparing or mean.
To restrain within certain limits; to bound; to restrict to a scant allowance.
A period of time spent doing or being something; a spell.
Limit; bound; restraint; extent.

ex.ja: 政治的に不穏な空気が流れていた。

ex.ja: 社会的不安を取り除くことが大切です。

Unskilled; inexperienced.
An examination involving material not previously seen or studied.

note.ja: un（否定）+ seen（見られた）。「目に見えない」。

en: A male or female attendant who serves customers at their tables in a restaurant, café or similar.
Someone who waits for somebody or something; a person who is waiting.
To work as a waiter.

waiter.ety:

Feminine form waitress first recorded 1834.
The London Stock Exchange sense harks back to the early days of trading in coffee-shops.

ex.en: Waiter, please bring me another glass of beer.
ex.ja: 店員さん、もう一杯ビールを持ってきてください。

ex.en: Waiter, please give me a cup of tea.
ex.ja: ボーイさん、紅茶を一杯ください。

ex.ja: 彼はすぐその仕事に飽きるだろう。

ex.ja: 私たちは彼の長話にうんざりしている。

The sufferings of Jesus Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane (often capitalized).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 astron（星）+ nautēs（船乗り）。「星の船乗り」→「宇宙飛行士」。nautical（航海の）と同じ。

ex.ja: ついに彼女は権力の座を手に入れた。

attendant.ety: From Middle English attendant, attendaunt, from Old French attendant. By surface analysis, attend + -ant.

ex.ja: 私はフライトアテンダントの職につきたいです。

To use something (e.g., a competitor's product) as a standard to improve one's own thing.

benchmark.ety: From bench + mark. First use appears c. 1842. Originally a mark cut into a stone by land surveyors to secure a bench (from land surveying jargon in the 19th century, meaning a type of bracket), to mount measuring equipment. The figurative sense first appears c. 1884.

To engage in a short period of excessive consumption, especially of excessive alcohol or media consumption.

ex.ja: ストレスでやけ食いをされる方も多いと思います。

ex.ja: ブレーカー上げてくればいいの。早く！

ex.ja: 見事な景色だ。

ex.en: The scenery's supposed to be breathtaking.
ex.ja: 景色もすばらしいはずよ。

note.ja: breath（息）+ taking（奪う）。「息を奪うほどの」→「息をのむような」。

en: A place abounding with shrubs where animals may browse.

note.ja: browse（見て回る）+ -ing。もとは「家畜が若葉を食べ歩く」→「ぶらぶら見る・閲覧」。

en: The state of being brutal.
A cruel or savage act.

From brutal + -ity.

ex.en: The police brutality incidents nearly set off a riot.
ex.ja: 警官による暴行事件はあやうく暴動に火をつけるところでした。

note.ja: brutal + -ity。ラテン語 brutus（鈍い・獣のような）。「残忍さ」。brute と同じ。

en: Any formal system in which symbolic expressions are manipulated according to fixed rules.
Differential calculus and integral calculus considered as a single subject.

calculus.ety:
* Borrowed from Latin calculus (“a pebble or stone used as reckoning counters in abacus”), diminutive of calx (“limestone”) + -ulus.
* Mathematical topic is from differential calculus.

ex.en: I'll pay you back with my calculus notes.
ex.ja: お返しに微積分のノートを貸してあげるわ。

ex.en: Learning calculus requires a lot of practice.
ex.ja: 微積分を学ぶには、練習問題をたくさんこなす必要があります。

note.ja: ラテン語 calculus（小石）から。小石で計算したことから「計算法・微積分」、体内の石 →「結石」。calculate と同じ。

en: Not concerned or worried (about).
Not giving sufficient attention or thought, especially concerning the avoidance of harm or mistakes.

careless.ety:

From Middle English careles, from Old English carlēas (“careless, reckless, void of care, free from care, free”), equivalent to care + -less. Cognate with Icelandic kærulaus (“careless, negligent”).

ex.en: It was careless of her to forget it.
ex.ja: それを忘れるとは彼女の不注意でした。

ex.en: The accident was due to his careless driving.
ex.ja: その事故は彼の不注意な運転のためであった。

ex.en: He was rather careless to say the least.
ex.ja: 控え目に言っても彼はちょっと軽率だった。

note.ja: care（注意）+ -less。「不注意な」。

en: Any of the hereditary social classes and subclasses of South Asian societies or similar found historically in other cultures.
A separate and fixed order or class of persons in society who chiefly associate with each other.

caste.ety: Borrowed from Portuguese or Spanish casta (“lineage, breed, race”), which the OED derives from Portuguese casto (“chaste”), from Latin castus (“chaste"; "chastity”), Coromines (1987) argues instead for a hypothetical Gothic form *𐌺𐌰𐍃𐍄𐍃 (*kasts, “group, collection of animals”), cognate with English cast, from Proto-Germanic *kastuz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ǵ-es-.

note.ja: ポルトガル語 casta（血統・家系）から。ラテン語 castus（純粋な）。chaste（純潔な）と同じ。

en: An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
A wine collection, especially when stored in a cellar.
To store (something, especially food or wine) in a cellar.

cellar.ety: From Middle English celer, seler, from Anglo-Norman celer, Old French celier (modern cellier), from Late Latin cellārium, from Latin cella. Doublet of cellarium. See native English cleve.

ex.en: He brought our TV set down to the cellar.
ex.ja: パパは、テレビを地下室に持ってきたの。

ex.en: That team is always in the cellar.
ex.ja: あのチームはいつも最下位だ。

ex.en: Our team is in the cellar.
ex.ja: わがチームは最下位だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 cellarium（貯蔵室）から。cella（小部屋）。cell と同じ。「地下室」。

en: Of or relating to the brain, cerebrum, or cerebral cortex.
Intellectual rather than emotional or physical.

cerebral.ety: Borrowing from French cérébral, from Latin cerebrum (“a brain”); equivalent to cerebrum + -al.

ex.en: I had a cerebral contusion.
ex.ja: 私は脳挫傷を起こした。

note.ja: ラテン語 cerebrum（脳）から。「大脳の」→「知的な」。

ja: シュプレヒコールを上げる

en: To sing, especially without instruments, and as applied to monophonic and pre-modern music.
To sing or intone sacred text.
Type of singing done generally without instruments and harmony.
A short and simple melody to which unmetrical psalms, etc., are sung or recited.

chant.ety: From Middle English chaunten, from Old French chanter, from Latin cantāre (“sing”). Doublet of cant.

ex.en: The children chanted, "Rain, rain, go away. Come again another day."
ex.ja: 子供たちは歌った。「雨よ、雨よ、遠くに行ってしまえ。また別の日に来なさい」

note.ja: ラテン語 cantare（歌う）から古フランス語を経た語。「唱える・詠唱」。enchant（魔法をかける ＝ 歌いかける）も同じ。

en: Noticeably happy and optimistic.
Bright and pleasant.

cheerful.ety: From Middle English chereful, cherful, equivalent to cheer + -ful.

ex.en: He is not the cheerful man he was.
ex.ja: 彼は昔の陽気な人でなくなっている。

ex.en: Whether sick or well, she is always cheerful.
ex.ja: 病気であろうと健康であろうと、彼女はいつも快活だ。

ex.en: Come what may, we must remain cheerful.
ex.ja: 何ごとが起ころうと、いつも快活でいなければならない。

note.ja: cheer（元気）+ -ful。cheer はもと「顔つき」→「上機嫌」。「陽気な」。

en: Of or relating to the cinema.
Resembling a professional motion picture.
A cut scene.
A short film promoting a video game or such type of franchise, often featuring its characters or universe

note.ja: cinema（映画）+ -tic。ギリシャ語 kinēma（動き）。kinetic（運動の）と同じ。

en: A rhetorical device in which a series is arranged in ascending order.
The culmination of a narrative's rising action, the turning point.
To reach or bring to a climax (in any sense).
To form the climax to; to be the climax of.
Being a climax species or climax community of organisms; able to remain essentially unchanged (in terms of the portion of the species in …

climax.ety: From Latin clīmax, from Ancient Greek κλῖμαξ (klîmax, “ladder, staircase, [rhetorical] climax”), from κλίνω (klínō, “to lean, slant”).

ex.en: The game came to a climax.
ex.ja: 試合は最高潮に達した。

ex.en: The audience sobbed throughout the climax of the movie.
ex.ja: 観客は映画がクライマックスの間すすり泣きした。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 klimax（はしご）から。「はしごの上」→「最高潮」。

en: A pit or other enclosure for cockfighting.
A site of conflict; a battlefield.

ex.en: The future pilot is trained in a mock cockpit.
ex.ja: 未来のパイロットは模擬操縦室で訓練される。

ex.en: It's easy to see the area's majestic topography from the cockpit of a helicopter.
ex.ja: ヘリコプターの運転席からなら、その地の素晴らしい地形を見渡すのは容易い。

note.ja: cock（雄鶏）+ pit（くぼみ）。「闘鶏場」→ 狭い場所 →「操縦席」。

en: The punctuation mark ⟨:⟩.
A rhetorical figure consisting of a clause which is grammatically, but not logically, complete.

colon.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek κῶλον (kôlon)bor.
Latin cōlon
English colon
From Latin cōlon (“a member of a verse of poem”), from Ancient Greek κῶλον (kôlon, “a member, limb, clause, part of a verse”).

ex.en: A colon is a punctuation mark.
ex.ja: コロンは句読点です。

note.ja: 「結腸」はギリシャ語 kolon（大腸）から。記号の「コロン」はギリシャ語 kōlon（手足・文の区切り）からで別語。

en: A joining together of minds or spirits; a mental connection.
Holy Communion; the Eucharist.

communion.ety: From Middle English comunioun, communyoun, from Anglo-Norman comunion or Middle French communion, from Ecclesiastical Latin commūniō (“communion”), from Latin commūnis.

note.ja: ラテン語 communio（共有）から。communis（共通の）。「親交」→ キリスト教の「聖餐式」。common と同じ。

en: A flexible sleeve made of latex or other impermeable material such as polyurethane or sheepskin, worn over an erect penis during sexual i…
Any of various forms of flexible sleeve or barrier, variously shaped for either penetrative or receptive body parts, made of latex or oth…

condom.ety: Unknown. Many speculations exist. Possibly derived from Italian guantone, from guanto (“a glove”).

ex.en: You used a condom for birth control, right?
ex.ja: 避妊はちゃんとコンドームつけてたのよね？

ex.en: Do you have a condom?
ex.ja: コンドーム持ってる？

ex.en: Do you have any condoms?
ex.ja: コンドームを持っていますか。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。18世紀から使われる語。

en: Either of the two heads of government and state of the Roman Republic or the equivalent nominal post under the Roman and Byzantine Empires.
Any of the three heads of government and state of France between 1799 and 1804.

consul.ety: From Middle English consul, from Old English consul, from Latin cōnsul.

note.ja: ラテン語 consul（古代ローマの執政官）から。consulere（相談する）。「領事」。consult と同じ。

en: Someone who competes with one or more other people.
Someone who has a viable chance of winning a competition.

note.ja: contend（争う）+ -er。con + tendere（伸ばす）。「力を伸ばし合う人」→「競争者・候補」。

en: A deep, slightly bluish red.
Having a deep red colour.
Immodest.
To become crimson or deep red; to blush.
To dye with crimson or deep red; to redden.

crimson.ety:
PIE word
 *kʷŕ̥mis
Late Middle English cremesyn, from obsolete French cramoisin or Old Spanish cremesín, from Arabic قِرْمِز (qirmiz), from Classical Persian کرمست (kirmist), from Middle Persian; see Proto-Indo-Iranian *kŕ̥miš. Cognate with Sanskrit कृमिज (kṛmija). Doublet of kermes; also see carmine.

ex.en: As the sun sets, the sky turns a beautiful crimson.
ex.ja: 日が沈む頃には、空が美しい茜色に染まる。

ex.en: As the sun sets, the sky turns a beautiful crimson color.
ex.ja: 日が沈む頃には、空が美しい茜色に染まる。

ex.en: The crimson flowers will bloom in January.
ex.ja: その紅の花は一月に咲きます。

note.ja: アラビア語 qirmiz（エンジムシ：赤い染料をとる虫）から。「深紅」。

en: A secret supporter or follower.
Secret or covert.

crypto.ety: All senses trace back to clippings of words derived from the prefix crypto-, developed at various times in the 20th and 21st centuries. During the 2010s and 2020s, the "cryptocurrency" sense has become the dominant sense. The "cryptography" sense predates that one; thus, a computer or math geek in earlier decades would be referring to cryptography when using this word. The "secret supporter or follower" sense is clipped from such terms as cryptofascist and cryptocommunist. The several informal senses in medicine referring to several microbe genera or the diseases they cause have existed since

ex.en: I don't mess with crypto anymore.
ex.ja: もう仮想通貨には手を出さない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kryptos（隠れた）から。cryptography（暗号）の短縮で「暗号資産」。crypt（地下室）と同じ。

en: Of a person, cultured, refined, educated.
Of a plant, grown by cultivation (not wild).

ex.en: She cultivated her mind by reading many books.
ex.ja: 彼女は大量の本を読んで精神を陶冶した。

ex.en: Good habits should be cultivated in childhood.
ex.ja: 良い習慣は子供時代に養うべきである。

ex.en: They cultivated the land.
ex.ja: かれらは土地をたがやした。

note.ja: cultivate（耕す・育てる）+ -ed。「栽培された」→ 心を耕した「教養のある」。culture と同じ。

en: Having curls.
Curling in a direction, as opposed to straight (quotation marks or apostrophes)
a person or animal with curly hair.

curly.ety:

English curl
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English curly
From curl + -y.

ex.en: Her hair is black, short and curly.
ex.ja: 髪は黒くて、短くてくるんとカールしてるんだ。

ex.en: Her hair is naturally curly.
ex.ja: 彼女の髪は天然パーマだ。

ex.en: He has curly hair.
ex.ja: 彼は巻き毛だ。

note.ja: curl（巻き毛）+ -y。「巻き毛の」。

en: The act of reducing in rank, character, or reputation, or of abasing; a lowering from one's standing or rank in office or society
The state of being reduced in rank, character, or reputation; baseness; moral, physical, or intellectual degeneracy; disgrace; abasement;…

ex.en: Will humanity be able to prevent the degradation of ecosystems?
ex.ja: 人類は生態系の退化を防ぐことができるだろうか？

note.ja: degrade（劣化させる）+ -ation。de（下へ）+ gradus（段階）。「段階を下げること」→「劣化・低下」。grade と同じ grad。

en: A disdainful indication that something is obvious.
An indication of mock stupidity.

duh.ety: Imitative, indicating stupidity by mocking the speech of an intellectually disabled person.

ex.en: All I can say is, "well, yeah, duh."
ex.ja: そりゃそうだろとしか言えない。

note.ja: あきれたときの声を表す擬声語。「当たり前だろ」。

en: Any of various green gemstones, especially a green transparent form of beryl, highly valued as a precious stone.
Emerald green, a colour.
Of a rich green colour.
To ornament with, or as if with, emeralds; to make green.

emerald.ety:
Etymology tree
Semiticbor.
Ancient Greek σμάραγδος (smáragdos)bor.
Latin smaragdus
Vulgar Latin *smaralda
Old French esmeraudebor.
Middle English emeraude
English emerald
From Middle English emeraude, borrowed from Old French esmeraude, from Vulgar Latin *smaralda, *smaraldus, *smaraudus, variant of Latin smaragdus, from Ancient Greek σμάραγδος (smáragdos), μάραγδος (máragdos), from a Semitic language. Compare Hebrew בָּרֶקֶת (bāréqeṯ, “emerald, flashing gem”), Akkadian 𒁀𒊏𒄣 (baraqu, literally “scintillation”), Arabic بَرْق (barq, literally “flashing”), Egyptian bwyrqꜣ (literally “to sparkle”):

ex.en: Dorothy and her friends continued their journey heading for Emerald city.
ex.ja: ドロシーたちはエメラルドの都を目指して旅を続けた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 smaragdos（緑の宝石）から古フランス語を経た語。

en: The condition of a system in which competing influences are balanced, resulting in no net change.
Mental balance.

equilibrium.ety: From Latin aequilībrium, from equal + lībra (“balance”).

note.ja: ラテン語 aequus（等しい）+ libra（天秤）。「天秤が等しくつり合った状態」→「均衡」。equal、deliberate と同じ。

en: In a manner which makes the fact or conclusion evident; obviously; as may be clearly inferred.
Apparently.

evidently.ety: From Middle English evidently, evydently; equivalent to evident + -ly.

ex.en: He was evidently surprised when he came across me.
ex.ja: たまたま私に出会ったとき彼は明らかに驚いていた。

ex.en: Evidently, it's going to rain tomorrow.
ex.ja: どうやら明日は雨になりそうだ。

ex.en: Evidently, he's made a mistake.
ex.ja: 明らかに彼はミスをした。

note.ja: evident（明らかな）+ -ly。e + videre（見る）。「見るからに」→「明らかに」。evidence と同じ。

en: Having fame; famous or noted.

famed.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-der.
Proto-Indo-European *bʰéh₂meh₂
Proto-Italic *fāmā
Latin fāmabor.
Old French famebor.
Middle English fame
English fame
Proto-Indo-European *-tósder.
Old English -ed
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos
Proto-Germanic *-ōdaz
Old English -od
Middle English -ed
English -ed
English famed
From fame + -ed.

ex.en: She is famed as a soprano.
ex.ja: 彼女はソプラノ歌手として有名だ。

note.ja: fame（名声）+ -ed。「有名な」。

en: An unborn or unhatched vertebrate showing signs of the mature animal.
A human embryo after the eighth week of gestation.

fetus.ety: A learned borrowing from Latin fētus (“offspring”). Doublet of fawn.

note.ja: ラテン語 fetus（出産・子）から。「胎児」。fecund（多産な）と同系。

en: Without flaws, defects, or shortcomings; perfect.
To win a fight against (a player) without losing health.

ex.en: Your English is flawless.
ex.ja: 君の英語は完璧だ。

ex.en: Flawless precision is required in the measurements.
ex.ja: 測定には寸分の狂いもない精度が要求される。

note.ja: flaw（欠点）+ -less。「欠点のない・完璧な」。

en: The daughter of someone's child.

ex.en: My great-granddaughter is eight years old.
ex.ja: ひ孫は八歳ですよ。

ex.en: My granddaughter is still a baby.
ex.ja: 孫はまだ赤ちゃんなのよ。

ex.en: Along comes the grandmother and sees her granddaughter.
ex.ja: すると、たまたま少女のおばあちゃんが通りかかる。

note.ja: grand（一世代離れた）+ daughter（娘）。「孫娘」。

en: A sport involving the performance of sequences of movements requiring physical strength, flexibility, and kinesthetic awareness.
Complex intellectual or artistic exercises or feats of physical agility.

gymnastics.ety: From gymnastic: see -ics; from Latin gymnasticus, from Ancient Greek γυμναστικός (gumnastikós), from γυμναστής (gumnastḗs, “athlete, gymnast”), from γῠμνᾰ́ζω (gŭmnắzō, “to train, exercise”), from γυμνός (gumnós, “naked”), because Greek athletes trained naked. By surface analysis, gymnast + -ics.

ex.en: He is good at gymnastics.
ex.ja: 彼は体操が得意だ。

ex.en: Tom is a gymnastics teacher.
ex.ja: トムは体操の先生だ。

ex.en: It's time for gymnastics!
ex.ja: 体操の時間です！

note.ja: ギリシャ語 gymnazein（裸で鍛える）から。gymnos（裸の）。古代ギリシャでは裸で運動した。gym はこの短縮。

en: By this means, action or process.

ex.en: I hereby declare the opening of the Olympic Games.
ex.ja: ここにオリンピック大会の開会を宣言します。

ex.en: I hereby beg to acknowledge your letter.
ex.ja: お手紙確かに落手いたしました。

note.ja: here + by。「これによって」。契約・宣言の文で使う。

en: Full of humor or arousing laughter; funny.
Showing humor; witty, jocular.

humorous.ety: From Middle English humorous (compare Medieval Latin hūmorōsus), equivalent to humor + -ous.

ex.en: He is of a humorous turn of mind.
ex.ja: 彼はこっけいな性質の人だ。

ex.en: The writer is very humorous.
ex.ja: その作家はユーモアに富んでいる。

ex.en: His behavior at the party was so humorous that I could not help laughing.
ex.ja: そのパーティーで彼の振る舞いはあまりに滑稽だったので、私は笑わずにはいられなかった。

note.ja: humor（ユーモア）+ -ous。ラテン語 umor（体液）から。体液の具合で気質が決まると考えられた →「気分」→「おかしみ」。

en: To bring upon oneself or expose oneself to, especially something inconvenient, harmful, or onerous; to become liable or subject to.
To render (somebody, or oneself) liable or subject to.

incur.ety: From Middle English incurren, from Anglo-Norman encurir, Middle French encourir, from Old French encorre, from Latin incurrere.

ex.en: My mistake incurred his anger.
ex.ja: 私の誤りは彼の怒りを招いた。

ex.en: My act incurred a blame.
ex.ja: 僕の行動は非難を招いた。

ex.en: The company incurred a deficit of $400 million during the first quarter.
ex.ja: 同社は第一四半期に４億ドルの欠損を出した。

note.ja: in（〜に）+ cur（走る）。〜に走り込む →（災難などに）「招く・被る」。

en: Inside, into, or within a building.
The interior of a building; the space inside buildings generally.

indoors.ety: From in + doors, originally two words, representing earlier within doors.

ex.en: Don't stay indoors because it is cold outside.
ex.ja: 外が寒いからといって家の中にいてはいけない。

ex.en: No weather was severe enough to keep him indoors.
ex.ja: たとえどんな天候であっても彼は家の中にはいなかった。

ex.en: I'd rather go out than stay indoors.
ex.ja: 私は室内よりむしろ外に行きたい。

note.ja: in（中に）+ doors（ドア）。「家の中で」→「屋内で」。

en: Communication, conversation.
Dealings between countries.

intercourse.ety: From Old French entrecours, from Late Latin intercursus.

ex.en: They lost some symbols of social intercourse.
ex.ja: 彼らは社会的交流の象徴を少し失った。

ex.en: Syphilis is an infection that can be transmitted through sexual intercourse.
ex.ja: 梅毒は性行為を通じて感染する病気です。

note.ja: inter（間で）+ cours（走る）+ e。間を行き来すること →「交流・交際・性交」。

en: In an interesting way.
It is interesting to note that…

interestingly.ety:
Etymology tree
English interesting
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English interestingly
From interesting + -ly.

ex.en: Interestingly, the way we understand words is not always that obvious.
ex.ja: 興味深いことに、我々がどのように単語を理解しているかは必ずしも明らかになっていません。

note.ja: interesting + -ly。「興味深いことに」。

en: Following the ideals of Marxism.
One that believes in or follows the ideals of Marxism.

en: A local law, passed by e.g. a city.
Prior to the Third English Civil War, a decree of Parliament.

To stir up a fire to remove ash or promote burning.
A prod, jab, or thrust.
An old, worn-out horse.

en: A small hole or perforation, caused by piercing.
An indentation or small mark made with a pointed object.
To pierce or puncture slightly.
To drive a nail into (a horse's foot), so as to cause lameness.

prick.ety:
From Middle English prik, prikke, from Old English prica, pricu (“a sharp point, minute mark, spot, dot, small portion, prick”), from Proto-West Germanic *prikō, *priku, from Proto-Germanic *prikô, *prikō (“a prick, point”), of uncertain origin, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *breyǵ- (“to scrape, scratch, rub, prickle, chap”).

ex.ja: その犬はその音を聞いて耳をピンと立てた。

ex.en: I have a pricking pain here.
ex.ja: ここがちくちく痛みます。

ex.en: I pricked up my ears.
ex.ja: 私は聞き耳を立てた。

note.ja: 古英語 prician（刺す）から。「ちくりと刺す」。

en: Fertile; producing offspring or fruit in abundance, applied to plants producing fruit, animals producing young, etc.
Similarly producing results or performing deeds in abundance.

prolific.ety: First use appears c. 1635. From French prolifique and its etymon Latin prōlificus, from prōlēs (“offspring”) + -ficus (“making”).

note.ja: ラテン語 proles（子孫）+ facere。「子を多く産む」→「多作の」。

note.ja: proportion（割合）+ -al。「比例した」。

en: Characterized by success.
Well off; affluent.

prosperous.ety: From Middle French prospereus, from Old French prosperer, from Latin prosperō (“to cause to succeed”), from Old Latin pro spere (“according to expectation”), from pro (“for”) + spes (“hope”).

ex.ja: 幸せで実りある新年を迎えられますように。

ex.en: That town looked prosperous.
ex.ja: その町は栄えているようだった。

ex.en: The Van Horn family was prosperous.
ex.ja: ヴァンホーン家は裕福だった。

note.ja: prosper（栄える）+ -ous。ラテン語 prosperus（望みどおりの）。「繁栄している」。prosperity。

en: A site for mining stone, such as limestone, or slate.
To obtain (or mine) stone by extraction from a quarry.
To extract or slowly obtain by long, tedious searching.

en: The action of exposing something to something, such as skin to the sunlight.
The act or process of declaring or describing something through either speech or writing, in nonfiction or in fiction; the portions and a…

exposition.ety: From Middle English exposicioun, from Old French esposicion, from Latin expositiō, from expōnere (“to put forth”). The sense meaning "exhibition" is a later semantic loan from French exposition.

ex.en: The exposition will be held for six months.
ex.ja: 博覧会の開催期間は６ヶ月です。

ex.en: I applied to be an attendant at the exposition.
ex.ja: 私は博覧会のコンパニオンに応募した。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ pos（置く）+ ition。外に置いて見せること →「博覧会・説明」。expose（さらす）。

en: To emit digestive gases from the anus; to flatulate.
To emit (fumes, gases, etc.).
An emission of digestive gases from the anus; a flatus.
One who is inflexibly meticulous.

fart.ety:
From Middle English ferten, farten, from Old English *feortan, from Proto-West Germanic *fertan, from Proto-Germanic *fertaną, from Proto-Indo-European *perd-.
The noun is from Middle English fert, fart, from the verb.

ex.en: If you eat this you'll fart a lot.
ex.ja: これを食べたらおならがいっぱい出るよ。

ex.en: The old lady is bound to fart.
ex.ja: おばあさんは必ずおならをする。

ex.en: Who's Tom? Oh, right. I had a brain fart.
ex.ja: トムって誰だっけ？あ、そっか。ど忘れしちゃってた。

note.ja: 古英語 feortan から。擬音的な古い語で、印欧祖語にさかのぼる。

en: Something which is believed to possess, contain, or cause spiritual or magical powers; an amulet or a talisman.
Sexual fixation to or arousal at something abnormally sexual or non-sexual, such as an object or a non-sexual part of the body.

en: Covered with fluff.
Light; soft; airy.
Someone or something that has a fluffy texture.
A babycino (frothy milk drink).

ex.en: The snow was soft and fluffy.
ex.ja: 雪は柔らかくてふわふわしてた。

ex.en: The bread was baked light and fluffy.
ex.ja: パンがふんわり焼けた。

ex.en: This towel is so soft and fluffy. It feels good!
ex.ja: このタオル、ふわふわで気持ちいいよ。

note.ja: fluff（綿毛）+ -y。「ふわふわした」。

en: An event undertaken to get money by voluntary contributions for a particular activity or cause.
A person who collects money from the public for some cause.

note.ja: fund（資金）+ raiser（集める人）。「資金集めの催し・募金活動者」。

en: Any device or machine, especially one whose name cannot be recalled, often either clever or complicated.
Any consumer electronics product.

gadget.ety: Unknown. First used in print by Robert Brown in 1886 (see quote in definition section). Might come from French gâchette or gagée, or from the French family name Gaget, an industrialist who produced promotional gadgets in collaboration with the project to build the statue of Liberty.

ex.en: These gadgets seem to be of no use.
ex.ja: これらの小道具は役に立ちそうにない。

ex.en: This is a great time-saving gadget for the housewife.
ex.ja: これは主婦の手間を省く便利な器具です。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。19世紀の船乗りの言葉で「ちょっとした道具」。

en: A single article of clothing.
The visible exterior in which a thing is invested or embodied.
To clothe in a garment.

garment.ety: From Middle English garment, garement, garnement, from Old French garnement, guarnement, from Old French garnir, guarnir (“to protect, fortify, clothe, garnish, adorn”), from Frankish *warnijan (“to ward off, refuse, deny”). More at English garnish.

ex.en: I wonder what materials the garment is made of.
ex.ja: 衣装の素材はなんでしょう？

ex.en: I can't find my garment bag.
ex.ja: 私のガーメントバッグはみつからないのです。

ex.en: 2. Sew together the shoulder of the garment body.
ex.ja: ２．身頃の肩を縫い合わせる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 garnement（装備）から。garnir（備える）。「衣服」。garnish（添える）と同じ。

en: Of or relating to geometry.
Increasing or decreasing in a geometric progression.

geometric.ety: From Latin geōmetricus, from Ancient Greek γεωμετρικός (geōmetrikós), from γεωμέτρης (geōmétrēs). By surface analysis, geometer + -ic or geo- + -metric.

ex.en: By architectural symmetry, Emmet means geometric symmetry combined with aesthetic uniformity.
ex.ja: 建築のシンメトリーで、エメットは美的統一性をもった幾何学的な対称性を意味している。

note.ja: geometry（幾何学）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 gē（土地）+ metron（測る）。土地の測量から。

en: Of, related to, full of, or exhibiting grace.
Kind and warmly courteous.
Expression of surprise, contempt, outrage, disgust, boredom, or frustration.

gracious.ety: From Middle English gracious, from Old French gracieus, from Latin gratiosus, from gratia (“esteem, favor”). See grace. Displaced native English hold (“gracious”). Doublet of gracioso and grazioso.

ex.en: It was gracious of you to accept.
ex.ja: お受け取りくださって幸いに存じます。

ex.en: The queen was gracious enough to invite us.
ex.ja: 女王は寛大にも我々を招待してくださった。

ex.en: She is gracious to everyone.
ex.ja: 彼女は誰にも優しい。

note.ja: ラテン語 gratia（好意）から。grac + ious。好意にあふれた →「親切な・優雅な」。

en: A smile in which the lips are parted to reveal the teeth.
To smile, parting the lips so as to show the teeth.
To express by grinning.

grin.ety: From Middle English grinnen, from Old English grennian, from Proto-West Germanic *grannjōn, from Proto-Germanic *granjōną. Related to groan. Compare to Middle High German grennen (“to mutter, complain”) and Danish grine (“to show one's teeth, to laugh”)

ex.en: He gave his sudden, goblin like grin.
ex.ja: 彼はいつものように突然不気味な笑みを浮かべた。

note.ja: 古英語 grennian（歯をむき出す）から。「にやっと笑う」。

en: A crowd; a throng; a multitude or great number of people.
A pile or mass; a collection of things laid in a body, or thrown together so as to form an elevation.
To pile in a heap.
To form or round into a heap, as in measuring.

heap.ety: From Middle English hepe, from Old English hēap, from Proto-West Germanic *haup, from Proto-Germanic *haupaz (compare Dutch hoop, German Low German Hupen, German Haufen), from Proto-Indo-European *koupos (“hill”) (compare Lithuanian kaũpas, Albanian qipi (“stack”), Avestan 𐬐𐬂𐬟𐬀 (kåfa)).

ex.en: I feel heaps better after a sound sleep.
ex.ja: ぐっすり眠った後はずっと気分がよい。

ex.en: She fell in a heap to the floor.
ex.ja: 彼女は床に崩れるようにして倒れた。

ex.en: Fan letters lay in a heap on the desk.
ex.ja: 机の上にファンレターが山と積まれていた。

note.ja: 古英語 hēap（群れ・山）から。「山・たくさん」。

en: A hummed tune, i.e. created orally with lips closed.
An often indistinct sound resembling human humming.
To make a sound from the vocal cords without pronouncing any real words, with one's lips closed.
To express by humming.
Synonym of hmm: a noise indicating thought, consideration, &c.
Synonym of um: a noise indicating doubt, uncertainty, &c.

hum.ety: From Middle English hummen (“to hum, buzz, drone, make a murmuring sound to cover embarrassment”); akin to Dutch hommelen (“to bumble, buzz”), dialectal Dutch hommen (“to buzz, hum”), Middle High German hummen (“to hum”), probably ultimately of imitative origin.

ex.en: Do you know anyone who hums while they work?
ex.ja: あなたの知り合いで仕事中に鼻歌を歌う人はいますか？

ex.en: I heard him humming in the shower.
ex.ja: 彼がシャワーで鼻歌を歌っているのが聞こえた。

ex.en: We all hummed to the music.
ex.ja: 私たちはみなその音楽に合わせてハミングした。

note.ja: 擬音語。「ハミング・ブーンという音」。humming bird（ハチドリ）は羽音から。
